title: 800 People, One Round Building — Home or Fortress? | China Travel Expert
description:
In the mountains of south-west Fujian stand some of the strangest homes in China: tulou — huge round (and square) earth buildings, three to five storeys high, with load-bearing rammed-earth walls and almost nothing but blank wall facing outward.

From outside they read as fortresses. Step through the single gate and it's a village: wooden galleries, laundry, red lanterns, kitchens, and an ancestral hall at the centre.

The biggest of them, Chengqi Lou in Gaobei village (Yongding), was finished in 1709 and packs four concentric rings inside one outer wall. In its heyday it supported over 800 people in that one building. UNESCO inscribed 46 tulou as a World Heritage Site in 2008.

🧭 Expert Tip: head for the innermost ring first — that's where the ancestral hall sits, and it's the quietest part of the building.

福建土楼：夯土外墙三到五层，外面看像堡垒，进门却是一个村子。最大的承启楼建于1709年，一圈套一圈共四环，鼎盛时住过八百多人；2008年46座土楼列入世界遗产。
